entry.title: Multiplier sequences, classes of generalized Bessel functions and open problems
entry.summary: Motivated by the study of the distribution of zeros of generalized Bessel-type functions, the principal goal of this paper is to identify new research directions in the theory of multiplier sequences. The investigations focus on multiplier sequences interpolated by functions which are not entire and sums, averages and parametrized families of multiplier sequences. The main results include (i) the development of a `logarithmic' multiplier sequence and (ii) several integral representations of a generalized Bessel-type function utilizing some ideas of G. H. Hardy and L. V. Ostrovskii. The explorations and analysis, augmented throughout the paper by a plethora of examples, led to a number of conjectures and intriguing open problems.

entry.title: Closed forms and open obstructions: the sample variance of three observations
entry.summary: The exact distribution of the sample variance for $n=3$ is known since Rietz (1931) for the uniform parent, and Royen (2007, 2008) gave a Fourier series for any bounded continuous parent. Neither settles which parents admit a finite closed form, nor which special functions it forces. In coordinates aligned with the cube diagonal the variance constraint becomes a cylinder and the cube cross-section a polygon with $S_3$ symmetry, hexagonal over the central band of the diagonal and triangular near either corner; the CDF is the volume of their intersection, the parent density entering as a weight. A closure hierarchy is then organized by the minimal function class containing the parent density: polynomial parents on any bounded interval always close in elementary terms, a theorem for the whole class; in the negative direction a single explicit parent already suffices, and for a rational one we prove the CDF is not elementary, the obstruction being an irreducible dilogarithmic part. Beyond those two theorems the hierarchy is a set of example-specific obstructions rather than a classification: for an algebraic parent the radial first-kind differential is shown non-elementary on a genus-two curve, and the exponential row is a conjecture supported by the Bessel structure of its radial integral. For the uniform parent we obtain a two-piece formula bifurcating at $Y=1/4$, where the variance disk first circumscribes the hexagonal cross-section at the cube center. For the singular arcsine parent we derive both endpoint laws in closed form and give a six-term approximation accurate to about $10^{-3}$, an accuracy Royen's universal series reaches at about a hundred terms.

entry.title: Turán type inequalities for oscillatory special functions
entry.summary: In this paper our aim is to prove a conjecture of Á. Baricz on Bessel functions of the first kind, which improves the classical Turán type inequality for Bessel functions of the first kind proved by O. Szász. The idea is to consider the normalized Turán expression for Bessel functions of the first kind and to show that between two consecutive zeros of the Bessel functions of the first kind the branch of this normalized Turán expression has a local minimum, and the minimum values form a strictly increasing convergent sequence, whose terms are strictly decreasing with respect to the order. Moreover, we extend this result to general Bessel functions and regular Coulomb wave functions, and we use a similar approach to show sharp Turán type inequalities for modified Bessel functions of purely imaginary order and parabolic cylinder functions. In addition, we prove a complex analogue of the result on Bessel functions of the first kind about the strictly decreasing property of the successive minimum values: an inclusion property in the complex plane of the Turán expression for Bessel functions of the first kind by using the subordinating factor sequence technique in the sense of H.S. Wilf. The techniques employed in the paper may be useful to treat similar problems where Turánians or normalized Turánians of other oscillatory special functions appear.

entry.title: Bounding martingale dimension by spectral dimension
entry.summary: We prove that the martingale dimension of a broad class of strongly local regular Dirichlet forms is bounded above by a small-scale version of spectral dimension. This resolves a conjecture of Hino for this class of spaces, extending his earlier results beyond self-similar fractals. Our proof uses differentiation of energy measures to select good blow-up scales and construct approximately harmonic coordinates. We then study weak limits of their Euclidean image measures and combine an integration-by-parts argument with uniform Sobolev inequalities to establish the dimension bound.

entry.title: Optimality of the BCC lattice among 3D lattice quantizers
entry.summary: We study the problem of the best approximation (w.r.t. the optimal transport metric $W_p$, $p \in [1,\infty)$) of the three-dimensional Lebesgue measure on a domain of volume 1 by a discrete probability measure supported on a Bravais lattice. This problem is known as the quantization problem and it arises in numerical integration, electrical engineering, discrete geometry and materials science. As the lattice size tends to zero and the cardinality of the support of the discrete measure tends to infinity, this reduces to the following geometric optimization problem: Amongst three-dimensional Bravais lattices with determinant $1$, which lattice minimises the $p$-th moment of the lattice Voronoi cell? Barnes and Sloane (1983) proved that the BCC lattice is optimal for the case $p=2$, which is known as the vector quantization problem in the signal compression literature. Bambah (1954) proved that the BCC lattice is optimal for the limiting case $p=\infty$, which is the sphere covering problem. Based on these results, Graf and Luschgy (2000) conjectured that the BCC lattice is optimal for all $p \in [1,\infty)$. Three dimensions is the critical dimension in the sense that in two dimensions the optimal lattice is independent of $p$, whereas in four dimensions it varies with $p$. In this paper we give support in favour of Graf and Luschgy's conjecture by proving that the BCC lattice is a local minimiser for all $p \in [1,\infty)$ and a global minimiser for $p$ near 2. While the conjecture asserts that the global minimiser is independent of $p$, we prove a bifurcation theorem which shows that the set of critical points depends on $p$ and that $p=2$ is a distinguished case. Our proofs combine results from discrete geometry by Barnes and Sloane (1983) and Conway and Sloane (1992) with optimal transport theory, the calculus of variations, bifurcation theory, and some delicate positivity estimates.

entry.title: Proof of the conjecture about inequality of $1/H$-variations of fractional Brownian motion along the equidistant and the Lebesgue partitions
entry.summary: We give an analytic proof of the comparison conjectured by Das, Łochowski, Matsuda and Perkowski for the fractional Brownian level-crossing constant: for standard fractional Brownian motion, $c_H>\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $0<H<1/2$ and $c_H<\mathbb{E}|Z|^{1/H}$ when $1/2<H<1$, where $Z\sim N(0,1)$. At $H=1/2$, both constants equal one. The main tool is Gaussian comparison under ordering of increment variances. It applies because truncated variation is translation invariant and lattice-submodular, as follows from its minimum-total-variation characterization. A tangent variogram produces Brownian motion with an independent Gaussian drift on the upper side, and a periodic Brownian bridge on the lower side. The former has an explicit stationary reflection rate. For the latter we calculate an integrated cyclic crossing count by first-passage Laplace transforms. Elementary hyperbolic, theta-series, and Gamma inequalities then give strict comparisons on both full parameter ranges. No numerical integration, simulation, interval certificate, or quantitative local expansion at $H=1/2$ is used.

entry.title: Some stochastic inequalities for weighted sums
entry.summary: We compare weighted sums of i.i.d. positive random variables according to the usual stochastic order. The main inequalities are derived using majorization techniques under certain log-concavity assumptions. Specifically, let $Y_i$ be i.i.d. random variables on $\mathbf{R}_+$. Assuming that $\log Y_i$ has a log-concave density, we show that $\sum a_iY_i$ is stochastically smaller than $\sum b_iY_i$, if $(\log a_1,...,\log a_n)$ is majorized by $(\log b_1,...,\log b_n)$. On the other hand, assuming that $Y_i^p$ has a log-concave density for some $p>1$, we show that $\sum a_iY_i$ is stochastically larger than $\sum b_iY_i$, if $(a_1^q,...,a_n^q)$ is majorized by $(b_1^q,...,b_n^q)$, where $p^{-1}+q^{-1}=1$. These unify several stochastic ordering results for specific distributions. In particular, a conjecture of Hitczenko [Sankhyā A 60 (1998) 171--175] on Weibull variables is proved. Potential applications in reliability and wireless communications are mentioned.

entry.title: Some new properties of the beta function and Ramanujan R-function
entry.summary: In this paper, the power series and hypergeometric series representations of the beta and Ramanujan functions \begin{equation*} \mathcal{B}\left( x\right) =\frac{Γ\left( x\right)^{2}}{Γ\left( 2x\right) }\text{ and }\mathcal{R}\left( x\right) =-2ψ\left( x\right) -2γ\end{equation*} are presented, which yield higher order monotonicity results related to $ \mathcal{B}(x)$ and $\mathcal{R}(x)$; the decreasing property of the functions $\mathcal{R}\left( x\right) /\mathcal{B}\left( x\right) $ and $[ \mathcal{B}(x) -\mathcal{R}(x)] /x^{2}$ on $\left( 0,\infty \right)$ are proved. Moreover, a conjecture put forward by Qiu et al. in [17] is proved to be true. As applications, several inequalities and identities are deduced. These results obtained in this paper may be helpful for the study of certain special functions. Finally, an interesting infinite series similar to Riemann zeta functions is observed initially.

entry.title: Order-Moment Transport and Hankel Determinants in Special-Function Inequalities
entry.summary: Scalar inequalities in an order parameter often arise as the $2\times2$ shadow of a stronger Hankel determinant statement. We record a moment-representation criterion: positive exponential and Mellin order representations, together with gamma-normalized completely monotone averages, generate totally nonnegative Hankel kernels, with strictness controlled by the support of the representing measure. The criterion packages the classical total-positivity mechanism as a recognition calculus for special-function inequalities, turning the order parameter into a moment exponent after the correct normalization. The applications include three named determinant lifts. First, we prove the positive Jackson $q$-gamma Hankel conjecture of Karp--Vishnyakova--Zhang: for $0<q<1$, the kernel $(x,y)\mapstoΓ_q(x+y)$ is $\mathrm{STP}_\infty$. This is an atomic Mellin-moment instance of the general criterion; the reciprocal sign-regularity problem for $1/Γ_q$ is separate and is not addressed here. Second, we answer Yang's continuous half-gamma Mills-ratio log-convexity question and strengthen it to strict total positivity, hence to all higher Hankel Turan determinants. Third, we treat Tricomi rays and the one-dimensional Coulomb regularization as all-minor Hankel determinant hierarchies. For the Coulomb regularization, the $2\times2$ minor gives the scalar log-convexity question recorded by Baricz--Pogany, and the full theorem supplies the corresponding all-minor strengthening.

entry.title: On the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue Problem
entry.summary: The classical Blaschke-Lebesgue problem seeks the convex body of minimal volume among all convex bodies of prescribed constant width. In this paper, we investigate the necessary conditions for volume minimizers of the $n$-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue problem via the inverse Gauss map and the inverse Weingarten transformation. We first introduce a generalized support function for hypersurfaces induced by the inverse Gauss map, characterize the Wigner caustic of constant width bodies, and accordingly construct convex bodies of constant width from prescribed functions. Building upon there results and applying the Brunn-Minkowski inequality, we establish a high-dimensional necessary condition: for almost every antipodal pair of a volume minimizer, one point is non-regular; at the other point, the minimum principal curvatures equals the reciprocal of the constant width. As an application, we provide a new proof for the two-dimensional Blaschke-Lebesgue theorem. Furthermore, we study the dimension-raising construction of Lachand-Robert and Oudet, and prove that every convex body produced by this construction satisfies our necessary condition. Finally, we put forward a conjecture stating that the sequence obtained by iterating this construction starting from a line segment yields minimizers for the Blaschke-Lebesgue problem for all dimensions.

entry.title: A complete solution to the reverse isoperimetric problem for $λ$-convex bodies
entry.summary: For a given $λ> 0$, a convex body in $\mathbb{R}^n$ is called $λ$-convex if it is the intersection of balls of radius $1/λ$. We show that among all $λ$-convex bodies in $\mathbb R^n$ of a given surface area, volume is minimized by the $λ$-convex lens, that is, the intersection of two balls of radius $1/λ$. This confirms a conjecture of Borisenko in all dimensions $n \geq 2$. Moreover, we extend this reverse isoperimetric inequality to all model spaces of constant curvature in arbitrary dimension and arbitrary $λ> 0$.

entry.title: Van der Corput inequalities for Bessel functions
entry.summary: In this note we offer some log-concavity properties of certain functions related to Bessel functions of the first kind and modified Bessel functions of the first and second kind, by solving partially a recent conjecture on the log-convexity/log-concavity properties for modified Bessel functions of the first kind and their derivatives. Moreover, we give an application of the mentioned results by extending two inequalities of van der Corput to Bessel and modified Bessel functions of the first kind. Similar inequalities are proved also for modified Bessel functions of the second kind, as well as for log-concave probability density functions.

entry.title: Kohler-Jobin meets Ehrhard: the sharp lower bound for the Gaussian principal frequency while the Gaussian torsional rigidity is fixed, via rearrangements
entry.summary: In this note, we provide an adaptation of the Kohler-Jobin rearrangement technique to the setting of the Gauss space. As a result, we prove the Gaussian analogue of the Kohler-Jobin's resolution of a conjecture of Pólya-Szegö: when the Gaussian torsional rigidity of a (convex) domain is fixed, the Gaussian principal frequency is minimized for the half-space. At the core of this rearrangement technique is the idea of considering a "modified" torsional rigidity, with respect to a given function, and rearranging its layers to half-spaces, in a particular way; the Rayleigh quotient decreases with this procedure. We emphasize that the analogy of the Gaussian case with the Lebesgue case is not to be expected here, as in addition to some soft symmetrization ideas, the argument relies on the properties of some special functions; the fact that this analogy does hold is somewhat of a miracle.

entry.title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for weighted curvature integrals in space forms
entry.summary: We establish two types of Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for the weighted curvature integrals of static convex domains in space forms. The first type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving three weighted curvature integrals, with the second Minkowski type inequality of Xia [Calc. Var. Partial Differential Equations 55 (2016), Art. 96] and the weighted almost Schur lemma of Li and Xia [J. Differential Geom. 113 (2019), pp. 493--518] as special cases. The second type consists of a complete family of inequalities involving two weighted curvature integrals, confirming a conjectured geometric inequality by Hu and Li [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 375 (2022), pp. 5587--5615]. The key novelty lies in observing that, via the orthogonal projection map, the weighted curvature integrals for domains in space forms admit a natural interpretation in terms of mixed volumes of Euclidean convex bodies, thus reducing the problem to the classical Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities in convex geometry.

entry.title: An $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling inequality in every dimension
entry.summary: Let $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ ($N\geq2$) be measurable with $0<|Ω|<\infty$, and let $u_Ω$ be its logarithmic potential ($N=2$) or Newtonian potential ($N\geq3$), normalized so that $Δu_Ω=χ_Ω$. We prove the sharp inequality \[ \int_Ω|\nabla u_Ω|^2\,\mathrm{d} x \leq\frac{1}{2Nω_{N-1}} \iint_{Ω\timesΩ}\frac{\mathrm{d} x\,\mathrm{d} y}{|x-y|^{N-2}}, \] where $ω_{N-1}=|\mathbb{S}^{N-1}|$, with equality if and only if $Ω$ is a ball up to a null set. In dimension two this settles the $L^2$ Ahlfors--Beurling conjecture of Fleeman and Khavinson. For $N\ge3$ it is equivalent to the scale-free bound that at most the fraction $(N-2)/(2N)$ of the total field energy lies inside $Ω$. We also obtain an explicit deficit identity, a sharp extension to bounded nonnegative densities, and consequences for torsional rigidity, Bergman analytic content, Brownian motion, and aggregation equations.
